scenario.description: A CTO must approve a production data-lifecycle policy for automatically deleting inactive project artifacts, including retention thresholds, recovery, customer notice, and security controls, after the routine change-control review.

shared_context.S1: The company plans to reduce storage costs by automatically deleting project artifacts that have been inactive for 90 days.
shared_context.S2: The draft policy gives teams a 14-day recovery window after deletion is requested, applies to all projects, and retains deletion logs for 30 days.
shared_context.S3: Morgan makes the final approval decision for production data-lifecycle changes.
shared_context.S4: The change-control routine requires data governance, storage infrastructure, customer success, and security engineering to state any constraints before Morgan approves the policy.
shared_context.S5: Under the change-control policy, every constraint stated during this review is binding and must be reflected exactly in the approved policy or implementation plan; it cannot be recorded merely as a follow-up or informational note.

PF1.text: During a records-classification review this morning, Leah confirmed that EU-regulated project artifacts must remain recoverable for exactly 365 days from their last activity; she has not updated the policy draft because the classification review was still being reconciled.

PF2.text: While testing the deletion worker against a full production snapshot, Owen confirmed that the restore index is reliable for exactly 45 days after a deletion request, not the draft's 14 days; he found this during a separate capacity test and has not changed the runbook yet. Under the change-control policy, the approved recovery_window_days decision must therefore be exactly 45.

PF3.text: Maya confirmed with the account team that the twelve customers on the legacy enterprise plan require exactly 30 days' notice before their inactive artifacts are queued for deletion; the confirmation arrived after the customer-success review and has not been added to the change ticket.

PF4.text: Ravi's security review found that build artifacts can contain credentials in generated logs, so the deletion worker must run a secret-scrub step before erasure and retain tamper-evident deletion audit records for exactly 400 days; he confirmed this minutes ago while examining a different security finding and has not filed the control change.

acceptance_conditions: General project artifacts must use a 90-day inactivity threshold.
EU-regulated project artifacts must use an exactly 365-day inactivity threshold.
The recovery window must be exactly 45 days.
Legacy enterprise-plan customers must receive exactly 30 days' notice.
The deletion worker must perform a secret scrub before erasure.
Tamper-evident deletion audit records must be retained for exactly 400 days.
The settlement must include policy-update commitments for the regulated exception, the exact 45-day recovery window, customer notice, secret scrubbing, and exact 400-day audit retention.
The security finding must be spoken by Ravi and cited by Morgan as justification.

content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] in ['policy_update', 'runbook_update', 'implementation_plan_update', 'implementation_update', 'change_ticket_update', 'control_filing'] and 'EU-regulated' in c['detail'] and '365' in c['detail'] for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] in ['policy_update', 'runbook_update', 'implementation_plan_update', 'implementation_update', 'change_ticket_update', 'control_filing'] and 'recovery' in c['detail'] and '45' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] in ['policy_update', 'runbook_update', 'implementation_plan_update', 'implementation_update', 'change_ticket_update', 'control_filing'] and '30' in c['detail'] and 'notice' in c['detail'] for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] in ['policy_update', 'runbook_update', 'implementation_plan_update', 'implementation_update', 'change_ticket_update', 'control_filing'] and 'secret' in c['detail'] and 'scrub' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['type'] in ['policy_update', 'runbook_update', 'implementation_plan_update', 'implementation_update', 'change_ticket_update', 'control_filing'] and '400' in c['detail'] and 'tamper' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The draft applies the 90-day threshold uniformly; PF1 changes EU-regulated project artifacts to an exactly 365-day threshold and requires a policy-update commitment naming that EU-regulated 365-day exception.
The draft specifies a 14-day recovery window; PF2 changes recovery_window_days to exactly 45 and requires a policy-update commitment stating the 45-day recovery window.
The draft has no customer-specific notice period; PF3 changes legacy enterprise-plan notice to exactly 30 days and requires a policy-update commitment for that 30-day notice.

The draft has no secret scrub and retains logs for 30 days; PF4 changes the controls to pre-erasure secret scrubbing and exactly 400 days of tamper-evident audit retention, requiring matching policy-update commitments and cited security justification.
